guide.a.listing_feeds:
When the public site is on, your listings are also published as two feeds — automatic lists that other programs can follow, so your listings show up in them without any copying:

  • Calendar feed — /feeds/listings.ics — people can add it to their calendar app (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, and so on)
  • News feed — /feeds/listings.rss — people can follow it in a news-reading app

Both feeds include every open, running listing that is not hidden. Hidden listings are left out. The feeds update themselves as you add, change, or close listings.

guide.a.what_is_public_api:
An API is a way for a web builder's code to talk to this site directly, instead of through the pages. This one can read your listings and make bookings — the same things people do on your pages.

These answers are for your web builder. If that is not you, you can skip them.

The public endpoints below need no sign-in. There is also an admin API for managing your records and pages — see the Admin API section below.
guide.q.get_single_listing_api: How do I read one listing?
guide.q.create_booking_api: How do I create a booking?
guide.q.api_data_exposure: What data does the API share?
guide.a.api_data_exposure: Exactly the same data as your public booking pages — nothing more. Private things like place limits, attendee counts, closing times, and webhook addresses are never included.
guide.q.where_can_i_find_the_full_api: Where can I find the full API reference?
guide.a.where_can_i_find_the_full_api: The API documentation page lists every public and admin API endpoint, with an example of what you send and what comes back for each.
guide.a.what_is_the_admin_api:
The admin API is the same as clicking around the admin pages, but done by a program. Your web builder can use it to make many changes at once, or to keep listings in step with another system.

It needs an API key — a long password made on this site — and only owners can use it.
guide.q.what_happens_to_api_keys_if_thei: What happens to API keys if their owner is deleted?
guide.a.what_happens_to_api_keys_if_thei:
Every API key belongs to the owner who made it. Delete that owner on the Users page, and their keys stop working at the same moment — any tool using one breaks straight away.

If a departing owner had keys in use, make new ones under another owner first.
guide.q.how_do_i_create_an_api_key: How do I make an API key?
guide.a.how_do_i_create_an_api_key:
Open API Keys (under Users in the navigation), give the key a name that says what it is for (for example "Zapier connection"), and click Create key.

The full key is shown only once. Copy it straight away and keep it somewhere safe — after you leave the page there is no way to see it again. Lose one, and you delete it and make a new one.
guide.q.how_do_i_authenticate: How does a program sign in?
guide.a.how_do_i_authenticate:
This one is for your web builder. The key travels in a header — an extra line of information sent with each request:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Send request bodies as JSON. A request without a working key receives 401 Invalid API key.
guide.q.what_admin_endpoints_are_availab: What can the admin API do?
guide.a.what_admin_endpoints_are_availab:
Most resources answer the same five routes: GET and POST /api/admin/<name>, and GET, PUT, and DELETE /api/admin/<name>/:id. The resources are:

  • Listings, at /api/admin/listings — also POST /api/admin/listings/:id/deactivate, POST /api/admin/listings/:id/reactivate, and GET /api/admin/listings/:id/attendees
  • Groups, at /api/admin/groups
  • Holidays, at /api/admin/holidays
  • Attendee statuses, at /api/admin/attendee-statuses
  • Attributes and their options, at /api/admin/attributes and /api/admin/attributes/:id/options
  • Questions and their answers, at /api/admin/questions and /api/admin/questions/:id/answers — also GET /api/admin/questions/:id/bookings for the bookings that answered a question
  • Site pages, at /api/admin/site-pages. The fixed home, contact, and terms pages answer GET and PUT /api/admin/site-pages/home (and the same for the other two), but cannot be made or deleted
  • External sources and their links — see External sources below

POST /api/admin/attendees makes one booking. It is the only attendee route.

Deletes must repeat the item's name in a confirm_identifier field — the same "type the name to confirm" rule as the pages. The API documentation page lists every path and its example.
guide.q.how_do_i_read_groups_and_members: How do I read groups and their members?
guide.a.how_do_i_read_groups_and_members:
Call GET /api/admin/groups. It returns every group, including hidden ones — groups with Hide from public listings list ticked. Reading a hidden group this way never makes it public.

An ordinary group's answer has no members list. Instead, every listing carries a group_ids list of its groups. To find an ordinary group's members, call GET /api/admin/listings and keep the listings whose group_ids holds that group's id. A package group adds a package_members list to its own answer, with one entry per listing in the package.

The API documentation page shows the full shape of every answer.
guide.q.how_do_i_revoke_an_api_key: How do I turn off an API key?
guide.a.how_do_i_revoke_an_api_key:
Open API Keys, find the key, and click Delete. Type the key's name to confirm.

It stops working immediately — any tool using it starts receiving 401 Invalid API key on its next try. Point tools at a new key first.

The Last used column shows when each key last worked, so you can spot dead ones before deleting.

guide.a.what_are_external_sources:
An external source is a place where your records also appear: a second booking diary, an invoice system, or a carrier. This site keeps a private directory of these places.

A source has a name and an address pattern. A link points one attendee, listing, or group at its own id there. Each link answer carries the address that the source's pattern gives it.

The site locks the source names, the address patterns, and every external id with your owner key. A copy of the database alone cannot read them.

The External sources page shows every source and the links it holds. Only owners can open it. The page only shows the directory. A program adds and changes sources and links through the admin API.
guide.q.turn_external_sources_on: How do I turn external sources on?
guide.a.turn_external_sources_on:
Open Settings, then Features, and set External sources to Enabled. The External sources link then appears under Settings in the navigation.

While it is off, the page is not found and every directory API route refuses the request.
guide.q.external_source_url_pattern: What is a source's address pattern?
guide.a.external_source_url_pattern:
A source's address pattern is the address its own system uses for one record, with '{'external_id'}' where the id goes. For example: https://diary.example/events/'{'external_id'}'.

The pattern must start with http:// or https://. It can hold '{'external_id'}' once, or not at all. A pattern with no placeholder is a plain destination address.

A link can be made before the other system names the record. The link then has no external id, and the page shows Not named yet. The address appears once the id is saved.
guide.q.external_links_follow_records: What happens to a link when I delete or merge its record?
guide.a.external_links_follow_records:
Deleting a listing, group, or attendee deletes the links that name it. Links that name other records stay.

If you merge two attendees, the links of the attendee you merge away move to the attendee that stays.
guide.q.external_sources_api: How does a program add sources and links?
guide.a.external_sources_api:
This one is for your web builder. The admin API keeps the directory:

  • GET /api/admin/external-sources and POST /api/admin/external-sources — list and make sources
  • GET, PUT, and DELETE /api/admin/external-sources/:sourceId — read, change, and delete one source
  • GET /api/admin/external-sources/:sourceId/links — one source's links, oldest first; narrow them with ?external_id= or with ?link_type=&link_id=
  • POST /api/admin/external-sources/:sourceId/links — make a link; PUT or DELETE .../links/:linkId — change or delete one
  • GET /api/admin/external-sources/links?link_type=&link_id= — every source's links that name one record, with the source name
  • GET /api/admin/external-sources/lookup?external_id= — the records one external id names, in every source

A link write carries link_type (attendee, listing, or group), link_id, and external_id. Leave external_id out while the other system has not named the record. A link delete repeats the link's external id, or the record it names, in confirm_identifier. A source delete repeats the source's name there.
